questions.q: What does Azure Key Vault actually manage?
options: Encryption keys, secrets, and certificates, all centralized in one service
Only virtual machine images
Only network firewall rules
Only user passwords for Microsoft Entra ID
questions.explain: Key Vault covers three distinct things under one roof: cryptographic keys, secrets, and certificates.

questions.q: How does AWS KMS's scope compare to Azure Key Vault's?
options: KMS is scoped specifically to encryption keys, while AWS splits secrets and certificates out to separate services like Secrets Manager and Certificate Manager
KMS and Key Vault have identical scope, managing keys, secrets, and certificates equally
KMS manages secrets and certificates but not encryption keys
KMS only works with Amazon S3 and no other AWS service
questions.explain: Unlike Key Vault, KMS is deliberately narrower — AWS handles secrets and certificates through separate dedicated services.

questions.q: What are the four core jobs that both Key Vault and KMS perform, at a conceptual level?
options: Generate, store, rotate, and gate access to keys
Compile, deploy, test, and release application code
Encrypt, compress, archive, and delete all customer data permanently
Create virtual networks, subnets, route tables, and firewalls
questions.explain: Both services generate new keys, store them in hardware-protected storage, rotate them on a schedule, and gate every use against an access policy.

questions.q: When an application needs to encrypt or decrypt data using a key stored in Key Vault or KMS, what actually happens?
options: The application sends the data to the service and asks it to perform the operation; the raw key itself never leaves the vault
The application downloads the raw key directly and performs the encryption locally every time
The application must email the key management team to request manual decryption
Key Vault and KMS cannot actually perform encryption or decryption themselves
questions.explain: Applications don't retrieve the raw key — they ask the service to perform the cryptographic operation, keeping the key inside the hardware-protected boundary.

questions.q: Why does centralizing key management in a service like Key Vault or KMS matter?
options: It gives an organization one place to see every key in use, enforce rotation policy, and audit exactly which identity used which key and when
It has no real benefit over every application managing its own keys independently
It is required only for companies with fewer than ten employees
It eliminates the need for any access control on encryption keys
questions.explain: Without centralization, keys end up scattered and hardcoded across teams and applications, which is exactly the unauditable mess these services prevent.
